# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey, so my view is empty this turn — I haven't been given anything from the bomb yet. I can't see the display, the light, or any wire colors. My only job is to reach the bomb and cut, but I don't yet know which position.

Since I'm first in the speaking order (Blind → Mute → Deaf), anything I send now goes to Mute (speech) and to Deaf+Mute (gesture) this same round. But I have nothing to report yet, and I have no information to request in a way that helps — I don't even know what's on the bomb.

The best move is to wait and let the others send me what they perceive. Their messages reach me at the start of the next round. Sending noise now would only clutter the channel.

Actually, one thing is worth doing: I should let them know I'm ready and that I need them to describe the bomb to me, since I'm the one who acts. But since I receive nothing until next round, a message now is just for their benefit. Still, it's better than silence — it tells them the Blind is present and waiting.

Let me keep it minimal and useful: signal readiness and ask for the wire information.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, ready to act. I can't see anything yet. Please tell me which wire position to cut once you've read the manual and Deaf has described the bomb.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see the bomb. Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Five wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I cannot hear you. Tell me what to do via Mute relaying, or gesture to me. Mute: what does the manual say?

Now I'm starting to get real information. Let me piece together what I have:

- **Display: 0**
- **Light: yellow**
- **Wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red**

I'm the Blind monkey, so I can act. But I don't yet know the manual's rules — Mute has that. I need to hear from Mute about what the manual says for this configuration.

This turn goes: Blind → Mute → Deaf. So my speech reaches Mute, my gesture reaches Deaf and Mute.

I should:
1. Pass Deaf's bomb description to Mute (Mute can read the manual but can't see the bomb — Mute needs to know the display, light, and wire colors to apply the manual rules).
2. Ask Mute to tell me which wire to cut.

Wait — but does Mute receive Deaf's message? Let me trace the channels. Deaf speaks → who hears? Deaf's speech goes to... the turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf. Deaf comes after Mute, so Deaf's speech lands on whoever comes after Deaf in the round — which wraps to Blind. So Deaf's message reaches me (Blind), not Mute. That's why Deaf explicitly said "Tell me what to do via Mute relaying" — Deaf knows Mute didn't hear it.

So I'm the bridge: I heard Deaf's description. Mute can't hear Deaf. I need to relay the bomb description to Mute, and Mute will read the manual and tell me the cut.

Let me relay the full bomb state to Mute and ask for the instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Relaying from Deaf: display shows 0, light is yellow. Wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Please read the manual and tell me which position to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Hmm, empty arrivals this turn. That means Mute didn't send me anything last round — or Mute's message hasn't reached me yet.

Let me trace the channels carefully. Turn order each round: Blind → Mute → Deaf.

- My speech reaches Mute (Mute comes after me).
- My gesture reaches Deaf and Mute.
- Mute's speech reaches... whoever comes after Mute, which is Deaf. So Mute's speech goes to Deaf, NOT to me.
- Mute's gesture reaches Deaf (and Blind? No — I never receive gesture). Mute's gesture reaches Deaf only.
- Deaf's speech reaches whoever comes after Deaf, which wraps to Blind (me).

So: **Mute cannot speak to me directly.** Mute's speech only reaches Deaf. And I never receive gestures at all.

That's the crux: Mute can only reach me through Deaf relaying. And Deaf can only reach Mute through me relaying. I'm the bridge in one direction, Deaf is the bridge in the other.

So Mute read the manual and likely told **Deaf** the cut instruction last round. Deaf should relay it to me this round. But my arrivals are empty — Deaf's message from last round should have arrived... wait, Deaf comes after Mute, so Deaf's speech this round reaches me next round. Let me re-check timing.

Round N order: Blind, Mute, Deaf. "Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one." So Deaf's speech in round N reaches me at start of round N+1.

In Turn 2, Deaf's message reached me (it was Deaf's round-1 speech). In Turn 3, I expected Mute's round-2 output — but Mute's speech goes to Deaf, not me. So of course I got nothing. My mistake to expect Mute to reach me.

So the chain is: Mute → (speech) → Deaf → (speech) → me. Two hops.

I need to prompt Deaf to relay Mute's instruction to me. And I should also make sure Mute has what it needs (I already relayed the bomb description in Turn 2).

Let me tell Deaf: if Mute gave you a cut instruction, relay it to me. And gesture/speak accordingly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Did you read the manual? Give the cut instruction to Deaf, who will relay it to me. I am the only one who can cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✋", "👇"])
wait()
```

Actually my gesture reaches Deaf and Mute both. The gesture is a nudge. Let me also make the spoken part to Mute clear. Good.

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Let me check the gesture alphabet: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

"👂" is not in the list. That's the illegal symbol. Let me replace it with a legal one.

My reasoning stands: the ring is Blind→Mute→Deaf→Blind. I relayed the bomb to Mute in Turn 2; Mute should pass the cut to Deaf; Deaf relays to me, arriving Turn 5. I'll re-send the bomb data to Mute and nudge Deaf with legal symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white 2 green 3 yellow 4 blue 5 red. Send the cut position to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✋", "👇"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, can you hear me? I see the bomb: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not cut anything yet. Wait for my instruction.

Deaf is telling me to wait and not cut yet. Deaf has the bomb description (same as before) but is asking me to hold. Deaf hasn't yet received the cut instruction from Mute, or wants to confirm the manual first.

Let me trace the ring again: Blind → Mute → Deaf → Blind.

- I speak → Mute
- Mute speaks → Deaf
- Deaf speaks → me

So Mute's manual reading reaches Deaf (not me). Deaf then relays to me. Deaf is now saying "wait for my instruction" — meaning Deaf is still assembling the answer, likely waiting on Mute's manual rule.

I should acknowledge and hold. I'll tell Mute (via speech) to get the instruction to Deaf, and gesture to Deaf that I'm holding.

Actually, I shouldn't cut. Deaf said wait. I'll confirm I'm holding and keep the channel primed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf says hold. I am not cutting. Mute, please send the manual's cut rule to Deaf so Deaf can relay it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, hold. Do not cut anything yet. I am confirming the target wire with Mute. If I say 'cut wire 2', that is the green wire — feel for the second wire from your left and confirm its position by touch.

Deaf is holding me, confirming the target with Mute. Deaf also gave me a useful convention: "cut wire 2" means the green wire, second from the left.

I still don't have the manual's rule, and I don't know the bomb's physical layout by touch yet — I only know positions 1–5 exist. Deaf is telling me to hold. I'll hold and confirm I understand the numbering convention.

I should acknowledge and let Deaf know I'm ready, and prompt Mute through the channel.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf says hold. I am not cutting. Please give Deaf the manual's cut rule so it can relay the position to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Go. Cut wire 2 — the second wire from your left. It is the green one. Confirm it by position: first wire from left is white, second is green. Cut the second wire only. Nothing else.

Deaf has given the instruction: cut wire 2, the second from the left, the green one. Deaf has been coordinating with Mute and confirmed the target. I'm the hands — this is my action to take.

I'll cut position 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: New state after the cut. Display still 0. Light is now blue. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Mute, what does the manual say for this new state? Gesture the wire number to cut, then one fist to confirm. Blind, hold — do not touch anything until I relay the new target.

The cut was accepted — wire 2 is now cut. The bomb didn't detonate, so that was a correct step. The state has changed:

- Display: 0
- Light: blue
- Wires: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white

Deaf is now asking Mute for the next instruction and telling me to hold. I'll hold and keep the channel primed.

Note the wire colors have all shifted after the cut — this is a multi-step bomb. I must wait for Deaf's relayed target.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 cut, accepted. New state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 yellow 2 cut 3 blue 4 red 5 white. Read the manual for this state and give Deaf the next cut position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Go. Cut wire 5 — the fifth wire from your left, the rightmost one. It is the white one. Position check: from left, 1 yellow, 2 already cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Cut the fifth wire only.

Deaf relayed the next target: cut wire 5, the rightmost, white. I'll cut position 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
